title: LLMs or JEPA?

rows.label: In one line
values: Predict the next token of text, one at a time, and keep going
Predict the representation of a hidden part of the input, never its pixels or tokens

rows.label: Training signal
values: Self-supervised on raw text: the next token is the label, so trillions of tokens need no annotation
Self-supervised on images or video: mask regions and predict their embeddings, with no labels, text or negatives

rows.label: What it outputs
values: Text (or code, or JSON), sampled token by token from a probability over the vocabulary
Embeddings. Text or actions come from a probe, a decoder or a planner built on top

rows.label: Handling the unpredictable
values: Spreads probability over a finite vocabulary, which works for discrete text
Encoders drop details that can’t be predicted; a latent variable can stand for the remaining choices

rows.label: Main data
values: Text and code from the web and books
Images and video: V-JEPA 2 used over 1 million hours of video and 1 million images

rows.label: Typical size
values: Billions to hundreds of billions of weights: Qwen3-8B has 8.2 billion, DeepSeek-R1 671 billion
Around a billion: I-JEPA’s ViT-H is 632 million parameters, V-JEPA 2 is 1.2 billion

rows.label: Planning
values: In text: the model writes out steps, or an agent loop calls tools and feeds results back
In the world model: V-JEPA 2-AC searches action sequences whose predicted state lands closest to a goal image

rows.label: Maturity in October 2026
values: Products: hosted APIs from many providers and open-weight models you can run locally
Research: papers, code and checkpoints from Meta FAIR; AMI Labs founded to build on it, with no product planned for years

rows.label: Licences of the best-known models
values: Provider terms for APIs; Apache 2.0 (Qwen3) or the Llama Community License for open weights
MIT for V-JEPA 2; CC BY-NC 4.0, non-commercial, for I-JEPA and V-JEPA

rows.label: Weak spots
values: Fluent but sometimes wrong; knows only what is in its training data or context; LeCun argues its common sense is shallow without experience of the physical world
Can’t say or draw anything on its own; robot success of 65% to 80% on pick-and-place in lab tests; most published results are on images and video

tip: They answer different questions. Use an LLM when the input or output is text and you need a working product today. Look at JEPA when the input is video or sensor data and you want a frozen encoder or a world model to plan with, and accept that it is research code. The two are starting to meet: LLM-JEPA adds a JEPA objective to LLM training, and VL-JEPA answers questions by predicting text embeddings.
